task: Connect the two blue Cat5e cables from the old phone block to new keystone jacks, join them with a patch cord, then test the link.

titles: Identify the two blue Cat5e cables
Trim and strip the first cable end
Punch the first cable into its keystone jack
Trim, strip, and punch the second cable
Snap both jacks into a surface mount or patch panel
Connect the two jacks with a patch cord
Test the completed link with a cable tester

reason: Only one blue Cat5e cable is clearly traceable in this photo, and neither cable is shown punched into an old telephone distribution block — the block visible is a loose keystone jack, not the distribution strip described in the step.
User reports one of the connectors feels warm and smells burnt. Possible overheating or electrical fault on the low-voltage wiring.

tools: 110-style punch-down tool (a small hand tool that pushes wire into a plastic slot and trims the end at the same time)
Keystone jack x2 (small snap-in network socket, T568B wiring, to match the color chart printed on its body)
Short Cat5e patch cord (a ready-made cable with plugs on both ends, any length 0.5–2 ft)
Cable tester (a two-piece device: plug one end of the finished link into the master unit, the other end into the remote unit, and watch the numbered LEDs flash in sequence 1–8)
